summary.storyTitle: Story 1: Pull and Status on the Record
summary.implementedScope: Fixed SV-01-PULL-STATUS-001 at the seam layer: the verified side-effect path was openThreadDatabase → fireThreadTouch → scheduler.touch, which in a background SDK can hang a first-touch catch-up drain (queue claims, provider calls, writes) off a thread-view read. The fix is a reads-only operation scope in shared/context.ts — runWithThreadTouchSuppressed runs a function under the current instance seam with the touch announcement replaced by a no-op while preserving the poke target and view config (and delegating to the below-SDK defaults when no seam is in scope, minus the touch). thread-view pull and status wrap their entire bodies in this scope, which structurally covers not just their own openThreadDatabase calls but also the owners' report surfaces status consumes — no test-only bypass, no signature changes to the frozen messages/turns domains, and write paths are untouched so first-touch catch-up still works everywhere it should. A new background-mode test leg extends TC-1.2/TC-2.5: pending work is manufactured through a manual SDK, then a fresh background SDK pulls twice and reads status; it asserts work rows / form states / view rows / boundary unchanged (full below-SDK state snapshot), provider fake at zero calls, repeated pulls byte-identical via full-result hash, repeated status byte-identical, and pending work visible through the read itself — after settling the scheduler (timeout + drainSettled) so a wrongly-scheduled drain would surface. The regression test was proven live: with the suppression temporarily removed it fails (the catch-up drain fires), with the fix it passes.
